export-explorer-stage-unassessed.reason: Adopt by the owner's direction of 2026-11-02, refs #289. Changes behavior on purpose. Old behavior: bench-tools export-explorer wrote each attempt in data/benchmark.json without an output-token lower bound. New behavior: each attempt carries "outputTokensLowerBound" after "outputTokens": the sum of the output counts its usage request rows record, or null when no row records one; it equals outputTokens whenever that is known, and this case's attempts gain "outputTokensLowerBound" equal to their output tokens. No other value changes. Rationale: counts are never negative and a partly recorded row only undercounts, so the sum is a true lower bound; the explorer shows output tokens as a lower bound, as it already does cost, instead of leaving a setup off the token chart when some attempts were only partly metered. Compatibility impact: a reader of data/benchmark.json sees one more key; src/lib/data.ts types it as a number or null.

export-explorer-publish-replaces-both.reason: Adopt for #198, porting the export of tools/export_explorer.py to the Rust export-explorer, part of #154. Diagnostics keep the Python program name export_explorer.py. By the repository owner's direction for #154, delegated through the migration's orchestration on 2026-10-19; resolved by #198. Changes behavior on purpose: publish() caught every exception, KeyboardInterrupt included, and restored the previous public/data and public/evidence before re-raising. The Rust command cannot catch a signal, because the crate forbids unsafe code, so the Python front ignores SIGINT while export-explorer publish runs: an interrupt in that window no longer stops publication. Both moves finish, or a failed move restores the previous pair as before, so public/ always holds a complete pair. Compatibility impact: Ctrl-C during the two moves publishes the new export where Python kept the old one; SIGTERM ends both as before. tools/test_export_explorer.py checks that SIGINT is ignored only while publish runs, and the cargo tests a_failed_move_restores_the_previous_pair, a_failed_restoration_keeps_the_backups and a_failed_first_publication_leaves_no_directories pin the restoration.

export-explorer-abbreviated-options.reason: Adopt for #215 slice A, part of #149, under #154's authority: the repository owner allowed pinned crates.io dependencies in rust/bench-tools on 2026-10-19, and #215 replaces main.rs's hand-written option parsing with clap 4.6.7 (derive, infer_long_args), delegated through the migration's orchestration on 2026-10-19. Diagnostics keep the program name export_explorer.py. Changes accepted input on purpose. Old behavior: bench-tools export-explorer matched a long option only when spelled in full and refused a prefix such as --ro, --f or --b as an unrecognized argument, exit 2. New behavior: clap's infer_long_args expands a unique prefix of a long option, as argparse does; an ambiguous prefix is still a usage error, exit 2. Rationale: #215 asks for argparse-style abbreviations through infer_long_args. Compatibility impact: command lines that spell options in full are unchanged, and a unique prefix that was refused now runs, toward Python: export-explorer has no argparse counterpart. Resolving issue: #215.

export-explorer-dot-digit-facts.reason: Adopt for #234, part of #156. Supersedes export-explorer-decisions.v6.json's refusal of -.5. Old behavior: clap 4.6.7 read a dash-led argument as a value only when it parsed as a number with a digit before any dot, so --facts -.5 was an unexpected argument, exit 2. New behavior: export-explorer reads a dash-led value as methodology and current-grading read one, through main.rs's attach_dash_led_values: a dash, an optional dot and a decimal digit, or a dash-led argument that holds a space, after an option that takes a value is that value, as Python 3.14's argparse reads it, so the command lists the evidence of the facts file -.5, exit 0. Rationale: export-explorer with no command replaces tools/export_explorer.py, whose argparse took --public -.5 and --public '-published dir', and the commands share export-explorer's options, so one reading covers both. Compatibility impact: a command line that was refused now runs; the attached form, --facts=-.5, still works. Resolving issue: #234.

export-explorer-exponent-facts.reason: Adopt for #215 slice A, part of #149, under #154's authority: the repository owner allowed pinned crates.io dependencies in rust/bench-tools on 2026-10-19, and #215 replaces main.rs's hand-written option parsing with clap 4.6.7 (derive, infer_long_args), delegated through the migration's orchestration on 2026-10-19. Diagnostics keep the program name export_explorer.py. Changes accepted input on purpose, toward Python 3.14. Old behavior: a dash-led value holding a letter, such as -1e5, was refused as an option, exit 2, as Python 3.12's argparse refuses it. New behavior: clap 4.6.7 reads -1e5 as a negative number in exponent form and takes it as the value, as Python 3.14's argparse does, which takes any argument that starts with a dash and a digit. Rationale: clap's allow_negative_numbers rule; keeping 3.12's refusal would need hand-written parsing #215 removes. Compatibility impact: a command line that was refused now runs, and no caller passes such a value; export-explorer has no argparse counterpart. Resolving issue: #215.

export-explorer-bare-double-dash.reason: Adopt for #215 slice A, part of #149, under #154's authority: the repository owner allowed pinned crates.io dependencies in rust/bench-tools on 2026-10-19, and #215 replaces main.rs's hand-written option parsing with clap 4.6.7 (derive, infer_long_args), delegated through the migration's orchestration on 2026-10-19. Diagnostics keep the program name export_explorer.py. Changes accepted input on purpose. Old behavior: the former parser had no end-of-options rule and refused --, exit 2. New behavior: clap reads -- as the end of options and, with nothing after it, ignores it. Rationale: clap's end-of-options rule; keeping the refusal would need hand-written parsing #215 removes. Compatibility impact: a command line that was refused now runs; export-explorer has no argparse counterpart. Resolving issue: #215.

export-explorer-help-with-attached-argum.reason: Adopt for #234, part of #156. Changes the first line of export-explorer's help, which this case pins by prefix, from 'List, stage or publish the explorer export from the current facts tools/export_explorer.py writes' to 'Export the current facts to public/ for the explorer, or list, stage or publish an export from a facts file', because this change deletes tools/export_explorer.py and export-explorer with no command now runs the whole export. Otherwise unchanged from export-explorer-decisions.v6.json: clap reads -hx as -h then -x and prints help, exit 0, as argparse does under Python 3.12 and 3.14. Compatibility impact: the first help line only. Resolving issue: #234.

export-explorer-help-with-equals-or-dash.reason: Adopt for #215 slice A, part of #149, under #154's authority: the repository owner allowed pinned crates.io dependencies in rust/bench-tools on 2026-10-19, and #215 replaces main.rs's hand-written option parsing with clap 4.6.7 (derive, infer_long_args), delegated through the migration's orchestration on 2026-10-19. Diagnostics keep the program name export_explorer.py. Keeps the exit code and changes the message. Old behavior: bench-tools export-explorer refused -h with = or - attached, such as -h=1, -h=, -h- and -h-x, as an unrecognized argument, exit 2. New behavior: clap would print help for them, exit 0, so main.rs refuses an -h before -- whose attached text, after any further h's, starts with = or - when clap is about to print help, with clap's error: prefix, argparse's message argument -h/--help: ignored explicit argument '1', and the subcommand's usage, exit 2. Rationale: argparse under Python 3.12 and 3.14 refuses these spellings with that message, exit 2, and prints help only for spellings such as -hx, -hhx and -hxh=1, whose attached text after the h's starts with neither. Compatibility impact: none for exit codes; only the diagnostic wording changes. This supersedes export-explorer-decisions.v5.json, which said argparse prints help whenever the text attached to -h starts with neither = nor -; argparse first skips further h's, so it refuses -hh=1 and -hh-x too. Resolving issue: #215.

export-explorer-current-mixed-billing.reason: Adopt by the owner's direction of 2026-11-02, refs #289. Changes behavior on purpose. Old behavior: bench-tools export-explorer wrote each attempt in data/benchmark.json without an output-token lower bound. New behavior: each attempt carries "outputTokensLowerBound" after "outputTokens": the sum of the output counts its usage request rows record, or null when no row records one; it equals outputTokens whenever that is known, and this case's attempts gain "outputTokensLowerBound" equal to their output tokens. No other value changes. Rationale: counts are never negative and a partly recorded row only undercounts, so the sum is a true lower bound; the explorer shows output tokens as a lower bound, as it already does cost, instead of leaving a setup off the token chart when some attempts were only partly metered. Compatibility impact: a reader of data/benchmark.json sees one more key; src/lib/data.ts types it as a number or null.

export-explorer-current-abbreviated-root.reason: Adopt for #234, part of #156. bench-tools export-explorer with no command now runs the whole export: it loads the current facts in process through bench_tools::current_grading::load_current and coverage_status, restores the evidence they link, stages, reads the record again and publishes, as tools/export_explorer.py did through a temporary facts file; this change deletes that front, and bun run data runs the command. Diagnostics keep the program name export_explorer.py. --r named --root in the front, whose only long options were --root and --public. bench-tools also has the hidden --restore, so clap refuses --r as ambiguous. Old behavior: the front's argparse expanded --r to --root and exported. New behavior: clap refuses --r, exit 2, because it also prefixes --restore, an option of export-explorer evidence. Rationale: the whole export shares export-explorer's options with its commands. Compatibility impact: --ro and longer prefixes still work; bun run data passes no option. Resolving issue: #234.

export-explorer-current-facts-without-co.reason: Adopt for #234, part of #156. bench-tools export-explorer with no command now runs the whole export: it loads the current facts in process through bench_tools::current_grading::load_current and coverage_status, restores the evidence they link, stages, reads the record again and publishes, as tools/export_explorer.py did through a temporary facts file; this change deletes that front, and bun run data runs the command. Diagnostics keep the program name export_explorer.py. --facts with no command: the whole export reads no facts file, so the option is refused. Old behavior: the front refused --facts as an unrecognized argument, and bench-tools export-explorer with no command refused with 'give one command: evidence, stage or publish'; both exit 2. New behavior: no command runs the whole export, which takes only --root and --public and reads BASE_PATH, as the front did; --facts, --base-path, --stage or --restore without a command is refused, naming the option, exit 2. Rationale: the front's command line moves to bench-tools. Compatibility impact: no caller ran export-explorer without a command. Resolving issue: #234.

export-explorer-help-before-invalid-shor.reason: Adopt for #268, part of #156, whose delivery plan ports each Python command line to bench-tools with argparse's arguments and exit codes. bench-tools export-explorer: --help before -h=1 prints the help and exits 0, because argparse acts on --help as soon as it reads it. Changes behavior on purpose. Old behavior: tools/export_explorer.py, deleted in 6bef4fb04, printed argparse's help and exited 0, run from its last revision, where bench-tools refused the later -h=1 with exit 2. New behavior: bench-tools export-explorer prints clap's help and exits 0; main.rs refuses -h, or a run of h's, with an attached = or - argument only when it is the first help before --, for every subcommand. Rationale: argparse acts on the first help it reads, so an earlier --help, or a unique prefix of it such as --hel, wins over a later -h=1. Compatibility impact: the exit code now matches the deleted Python's; only the help wording differs, as for every bench-tools help. Python 3.12 and 3.14 agree. Resolving issue: #268.
